analysis: Reviewed the two base-text units of provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift (lines 1756-3038). The PR change is test-only: a head-side addition at ~3140-3240 adds tests for SSDWholeRootMaintainer. They check that a remembered header-ownership verdict is dropped when a file's contents change, using the ctime/status-change signal, even when mtime and size are restored. They also check that a malformed lookalike later replaced by a real block is re-read and owned. No production source is in the supplied units, so I could not examine the maintainer's verdict cache implementation. The visible base tests cover SSD ready receipts, write-failure barriers, staging reservation release, whole-root TTL and budget eviction, and epoch preservation. They exercise the T-041 mitigations: HMAC lookup tags, DBK3 authentication, TTL/LRU, staging reservation release, and the disk reserve. They add no new attack surface and weaken no assertions in the visible range. The new tests suggest a production change that caches header-ownership verdicts in the whole-root maintainer, which deletes files by TTL and budget. The security-relevant questions are whether a cached verdict could wrongly authorize deletion of, or skip deletion of, a replaced or lookalike file, and whether the cache key (size, mtime, ctime, inode) is sound. I could not verify the production implementation here, so integration should review SSDWholeRootMaintainer's verdict cache. The excerpt is truncated, so the remaining new tests were not seen. No concrete regression is identified from the supplied evidence.
